thread:
incident-bot: ALERT — High latency p99 detected for tenant OrchidHealth on eu-west-1 dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-47). p95 also elevated. Count: 4.2% requests hitting >1200ms. Paging pager:raj (oncall).

raj (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledging the page. What's the customer impact? Lina, can you confirm SLA? :phone:

lina (customer-success): OrchidHealth is on our Enterprise Dedicated tier with 99.9% p99 SLA. They've reported slow UI earlier from their side ~10m ago but didn't open a ticket yet. They're in EU and have heavy daytime traffic. I'm calling now and will update.

maria (sre): quick telemetry: p50 ~80ms, p95 ~450ms, p99 ~1.4s for the last 5m. Error rate OK. Tail spikes correlate with long KV cache misses and occasional GPU queueing. Link to dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/metrics/orchid/dedicated/dp-47 (ops-only)

kai (runtime): adding detail — we've seen increased seq len for a subset of Orchid requests (avg tokens ~420, peak ~1200). That inflates KV reuse and causes longer GPU stall windows. Also one of the nodes in pool dp-47 is at 92% mem for the LLM KV cache.

raj (oncall): immediate runbook steps I'm starting: 1) put Orchid traffic into mitigation-mode (route to lower-burst SLA) 2) scale pool dp-47 by +2 nodes 3) apply temporary routing to fallback model-qt32 if compatible.

maria (sre): +1 to scaling now. I'll run the autoscale override. Command: 
```
# override autoscale for pool dp-47
redwood infra pool scale --pool dp-47 --add 2 --reason "p99 spike OrchidHealth"
```

kai (runtime): before scaling finishes (~60s), let's reduce batching window for Orchid to lower tail blocks. Config change: 
```
# set per-tenant batching ms
redwood config set --tenant orchidhealth --batching.window_ms 20
```
That will reduce batching and should lower p99 at the cost of token efficiency.

raj (oncall): doing batching change now. Maria, can you check node-level hotspots?

maria (sre): checking. Node r3-gpu-7 showing repeated GC stalls in kernel logs. Dumping last 200 lines: 
```
[INFO] kvcache miss spike at 12:08:02
[WARN] GPU queue depth surge
[ERROR] stalled batch id=4821 duration=1.12s
```
I recommend cordoning r3-gpu-7 and letting traffic drain to others.

kai (runtime): agree — cordon and redeploy. Command: 
```
redwood infra node cordon r3-gpu-7 --pool dp-47 --drain
```
I'll also enable the fallback model route for Orchid so we don't drop requests. Fallback: model redwood-llama-rlf-qt32, lower mem and quantized.

ben (sales-eng): heads-up — I'm on the call with the Orchid lead. They're seeing failed actions in their admin portal and users are complaining. If we do a fallback route, let me confirm compatibility with Orchid's prompt schemas (they use tool-calls). Might need to maintain function-calling surface.

lina (customer-success): on call with their ops lead Sam. Sam: "We can't accept degraded accuracy for some endpoints, but UI latency is killing product demos." He's asked for ETA on mitigation. I'll push for temporary maintenance window if we need full-tenant failover.

raj (oncall): timeline: batching change applied (12:09), autoscale override requested (12:09:30), cordon node started (12:10). Maria — confirm when cordon complete and pool scaled.

maria (sre): cordon complete, draining finished at 12:12. Node r3-gpu-7 removed from rotation. Pool scale succeeded at 12:13:15; 2 nodes added (r4-gpu-3, r4-gpu-4).

kai (runtime): fallback route enabled for Orchid at 12:13:40 for routes: /generate, /chat. Kept function-calls on for compatibility. Command used: 
```
redwood routing set --tenant orchidhealth --fallback redwood-llama-rlf-qt32 --routes "/generate,/chat"
```

raj (oncall): monitoring p99...

maria (sre): p99 dropped from 1.4s -> 760ms within 2m of actions. p95 back to ~380ms. Still above SLA target but trending down.

incident-bot: UPDATE — paging replicates: active duration 19m, current status: partial mitigation.

ben (sales-eng): Orchid wants an anticipated full recovery ETA. Based on current trend, any guess?

kai (runtime): with new nodes warm and fallback in place we can expect tail latency to stabilize in 10-15m, but if we see sustained high seq lengths we'll need to propose a long-term plan: dedicated node with larger KV cache or model quantization profile change.

lina (customer-success): told Sam we're aiming for <500ms p99 within 20m. He acknowledged but asked for written incident note afterwards.

raj (oncall): action list so far: batching window reduced, pool +2 nodes, node r3-gpu-7 cordoned, fallback route enabled. Next: monitor for 30m, if p99 >800ms escalate to SRE lead. Assigning ops-night (oncall) for handoff at +30m.

maria (sre): enabling extra retention of traces for Orchid for 1h to capture regressions: 
```
redwood trace retention set --tenant orchidhealth --duration 60m --level debug
```

ops-night (oncall): I'm taking the 13:00-17:00 handoff. Will watch and reach out if p99 rises again.

raj (oncall): thanks all. Lina/Ben please capture customer comms. I'll start a post-incident doc and link runbook items.

lina (customer-success): noted. Sam asked for a follow-up call in 1h. Scheduling now.

maria (sre): p99 steady at ~520ms after 9m. Closing active mitigation phase, keeping open for monitoring.

incident-bot: RESOLUTION CHECK — No further paging events in last 10m. If you were paged, please mark incident as acknowledged and add a short blameless note to the postmortem. :white_check_mark:

raj (oncall): closing warroom for now. Postmortem: I'll seed with timeline and attach logs + mitigations. Tagging @kai @maria for root cause follow-up (KV sizing + batching defaults).

lina (customer-success): Sam appreciated quick response. He'll wait for the postmortem and a plan to avoid repeats.

ben (sales-eng): I'll follow up on any contract impact with Pricing team, but looks like mitigation was fast enough to avoid SLA credit.

dev-deploy-bot: deploy redwood-runtime@v4.12.1 scheduled to dp-47 for KV-size tweak — ETA 02:00 UTC.

raj (oncall): noted. Thanks everyone.
